title.narrative: 2021-25 UNIR: BUILDING DEMOCRATIC AND PEACE CULTURES

description.narrative:
The general objective of the intervention is to i) strengthen the capacities (power and voice) of subnational public institutions (and of some estrategic citizen organizations) for they to become constructive conflict managers, and ii) to develop and strengthen the role of the impartial third party, in order to generate conditions for good governance and peacebuilding cultures at the local levels, especially on environmental and municipal issues.
UNIR has developed four action lines to implement the present contribution:
Action Line 1: GENERATION OF KNOWLEDGE AND INFORMATION ABOUT SOCIAL CONFLICTS Specific objective: To provide analytical information on social tensions and conflicts in the country, in order to contribute to a better understanding of national reality, so it can be used to in adequate decision-making processes that may contribute to an improved governance, enhanced democracy and the construction of a culture of peace in the country.
Action line 2: DEVELOPMENT OF CAPACITIES FOR CONFLICT PROVENTION: MANAGEMENT AND CONCILIATION Specific objective: Public officials and members of citizen organizations have strengthened their skills to contribute to i) a constructive and peaceful management of disputes and conflicts, and ii) an improved performance of an impartial third party for conciliation purposes.
(Incidentally, provention (and not prevention) is a neologism which means to provide individuals and/or groups with the necessary skills to deal with conflicts. It is learning on how to deal with the conflict, rather than trying to avoid it (conflict prevention).
Action line 3: CONSTRUCTIVE AND CONCRETE ACTIONS IN CONFLICT MANAGEMENT PROCESSES AND CONCILIATION Specific objective: To contribute to a constructive and peaceful management of controversies and conflicts which, hopefully, will generate reference cases to better guide future interventions of the responsible actors and strengthen the role of the third party.
Action line 4: DIALOGICAL PROCESSES FOR THE REENCOUNTER AND RECONCILIATION Specific objective: To contribute to the reconciliation and to a constructive/productive dialogue between representative groups of distanced and/or confronted sectors in order to strengthen their power and voice and ability to propose public policies for an improved and pacific democratic coexistence.

Det övergripande målet med insatsen är att i) stärka kapaciteten (makt och röst) hos subnationella offentliga institutioner (och hos vissa strategiska medborgarorganisationer) för att de ska kunna bli konstruktiva konflikthanterare, och ii) att utveckla och stärka rollen för den opartiska tredje parten, för att skapa förutsättningar för god samhällsstyrning och fredsbyggande kulturer på lokal nivå, Inte minst när det gäller miljö- och kommunfrågor.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
The year 2024 represented a critical and highly productive period for the project, characterized by significant achievements despite a challenging operational context defined by political tensions leading to general elections and a severe 46% budget cut. The partner demonstrated remarkable operational flexibility and strategic prioritization, successfully executing most planned activities by optimizing resources and shifting to digital formats where necessary. The decision, agreed upon with Sida, to reorient the project's final year (2025) towards the electoral-political context led to a consolidation and closure of processes initiated since 2022 during this reporting period.
Key results across the Action Guidelines
LA1: Knowledge Generation on Social Conflictivity
* Substantial Research Output: Successfully published and widely disseminated the in-depth research "La casa despojada. Conflictividad ambiental en Bolivia," with high-impact public presentations in three major cities, exceeding attendance expectations. The physical edition was exhausted, indicating high demand.
* Adapted Analytical Products: Delivered two high-quality analytical documents on social conflictivity (covering Jan-Jul and Aug-Nov 2024) instead of the planned three, extending their timeframes to provide more comprehensive analysis. These were effectively disseminated digitally, garnering hundreds of views and downloads, and were cited by national media.
* Innovative Tool Development: Concluded the methodological development and calibration of the Social Conflict Risk Index (IRC). While its launch was postponed to Q1 2025, its completion represents a significant advancement in predictive conflict analysis capabilities in Bolivia.
* Effective Virtual Dialogue: Successfully transitioned reflection spaces to virtual formats, subsequently reaching over 1,100 viewers through social media, thus expanding reach beyond the live participants.
LA2-1 & LA2-2: Capacity Development for Conflict Provenction and Extrajudicial Conciliation
* Targeted Local Impact: Effectively built capacities in constructive conflict management with 250 participants (57% women) from key public entities and civil society organizations in Cochabamba, moving beyond training to provide direct advisory support on latent conflicts (e.g., the urban waste tax in Tiquipaya).
* National Reach in Conciliation: Trained 243 individuals (73% women) in extrajudicial conciliation, including public officials from strategic institutions (INRA, Consumer Rights), academics, and civil society actors, strengthening access to justice mechanisms.
* Systematization Challenge: A draft systematization guide on constructive conflict management was not finalized due to staff turnover, representing a minor setback in institutional knowledge capture.
LA3-2: Extrajudicial Conciliation Processes
* Effective Case Management: Managed 39 conciliation requests, achieving full agreements in 15 cases (62.5% success rate for cases where parties attended), directly contributing to peaceful conflict resolution.
* Strategic Communication: Conducted a successful social media campaign on conciliation, reaching 59,000 users and generating significant interaction, raising public awareness of alternative dispute resolution.
LA4-1 & LA4-2: Dialogic Processes and Democratic Dialogues
* Exceptional Youth Leadership: This component stands out for its innovation and impact. Youth groups in La Paz, Cochabamba, and Santa Cruz designed and implemented five highly relevant initiatives (e.g., Memorial Green Area, Triviapaz, Coexistence Agreements, Emotional Backpack, Curucusí Campaign). These actions show strong local ownership and have been successfully institutionalized within public education directorates and universities, ensuring sustainability.
* Successful Multi-Stakeholder Dialogue: The "Tiquipaya Dialoga" process was effectively launched, engaging over 400 citizens, academia, and public officials in dialogue on solid waste management. The process generated concrete citizen proposals and an academic study as a base for public policy, successfully replicating the model from Tarija.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
